The founder approval matrix operates as a categorical lattice where each node represents a launch readiness state. Each department contributes a boolean evidence vector, forming a cross-departmental consistency check. The lattice is validated by verifying repository state (R, B, F), ensuring no duplication of prior work (CMD-067). The system enforces a minimum evidence threshold (E ≥ 0.9) for approval, failing when this condition is violated. The matrix ensures that all actions requiring founder/legal approval are explicitly listed, preventing unauthorized changes. The GSI Bayesian inference layer updates beliefs based on these verifications, while the GSE engine uses the lattice to transition between valid launch states. Failure modes include inconsistent evidence (C < 0.8) or unverified repository state (R = false).
